messages.subject: Get.real
parts:
Hello everyone,

First, what a great function name- get.real().

I am projecting density from an oscr model across western North America. I have about 4.3M cells of interest. For some reason get.real seems slow to predict, it took ~6 mins to predict on 100 rows, so extrapolating to 4.3M rows, it will take a very long time (I think >100 days..). Is this expected behaviour? Should I do something different, or is there a bug on my end?

Cheers,
Clayton


--

messages.author: 58a62321f08f30f8
messages.subject: RE: [oscr] Get.real
parts:
Hi Clayton,

 

Just to add to Dan’s comment:

 

I just went through this process for projections across New Hampshire. Turns out that for a given model, times scales pretty linearly with number of pixels. If you need maps of uncertainty, then it’s going to be time consuming unless you coarsen the resolution of the prediction raster or parallelize the whole thing. If you want a map of expected density, then you can compute that by hand (the time consuming part of get.real() is the computing the se using the delta method). Similar thing happens when projecting across large spaces using models in unmarked.

Subject: Re: [oscr] Get.real

 

Hey Clayton, did you try other sizes for the newdata? 200 or 300 rows?  I doubt it will scale linearly like you suggest, it probably has more to do with the fitlist size and complexity of the SCR model.

#say spdf is the data frame of pixel values for the whole area

                d.beta.ndvi_scale * spdf$ndvi_scale +

                d.beta.cc_scale *   spdf$cc_scale)

 

Probably worth adding a se=F argument for get.real().
